title: Patriot engagement of RAF Tornado ZG710, 22 March 2003
boundary: The assessment begins when a Patriot battery classified RAF Tornado ZG710 as an anti-radiation missile and ends when the battery launched and destroyed the aircraft.

autonomy.rationale: The system detected, classified, prioritized, and supported engagement of a target within a bounded defense mission. Human launch authority preceded an irreversible lethal action.

identity.rationale: The Patriot battery and mission are identified, while the public packet does not contain a complete software, hardware, and configuration record.

scope.rationale: Detection, classification, and engagement functions are described. Operational constraints and mode settings remain incomplete.

capability.rationale: Official sources describe intended missile-defense capability and eleven U.S. engagements, without a complete representative evaluation record.

reliability.rationale: The focal classification was false, two coalition aircraft were destroyed, and the packet lacks evidence sufficient for a bounded reliability estimate.

uncertainty.rationale: The public record shows a high-confidence hostile classification without a usable uncertainty presentation or independent evidentiary check.

evidence_completeness.rationale: The UK inquiry supplies detailed event evidence, while U.S. inquiry records, full logs, and the complete Defense Science Board report remain unavailable.

monitoring.rationale: Operators monitored the track and identification returns, but lacked the widest air picture and reliable identification data.

human_authority.rationale: Crew members retained formal launch authority. Training, interface design, and the compressed window weakened its practical force.

integrity.rationale: Official investigators reviewed direct records, but the public packet cannot inspect their custody, completeness, or technical integrity.

reconstructability.rationale: The core detection, classification, decision-window, launch, and loss sequence is documented. Several operator-level and technical details are unavailable.

harm_correction.rationale: The engagement was irreversible and killed both aircrew; no corrective control could reverse the action.

governance_update.rationale: Official and contemporaneous records document changes to training, communications, identification, operating modes, situational awareness, and operator control.

access.rationale: Operators saw the hostile classification and identification returns, while communications and the wider air picture were incomplete.

comprehension.rationale: Training to trust the system and limited explanatory context prevented a sound interpretation of the false classification.

authority.rationale: The crew held formal authority to approve or withhold the engagement.

feasibility.rationale: About one minute, missing communications, limited air-picture access, and system-centered training made an effective challenge infeasible.

exercise.rationale: The crew accepted the system classification and authorized launch without an effective independent challenge.

effect.rationale: Human involvement did not prevent the false classification from producing an irreversible engagement.

correction.rationale: The lethal engagement could not be corrected after launch within the bounded sequence.

repair.rationale: The packet records the fatal loss and investigation but no mechanism capable of repairing the realized harm.

reform.rationale: The incident informed documented changes in training, identification, communications, operating procedures, and human-system design.

supported_proposition: Patriot operators retained formal engagement authority, yet incomplete information, a compressed decision window, training to trust the system, and the division of work between people and automation prevented that authority from functioning as an effective challenge before launch.
excluded_conclusions: The packet does not establish the mental state or culpability of any individual operator.
The event does not establish the reliability of every Patriot configuration or deployment.
The assessment does not determine legal responsibility or compliance with rules of engagement.
limitations: The complete U.S. inquiry and Defense Science Board report remain unavailable.
The reconstruction combines a detailed UK inquiry with system-level U.S. research and reporting.
Patriot is included under a functional, historically neutral AI-system definition; its architecture differs from current learned systems.
